title: The Apocrypha helps only the reader the Spirit enlightens
setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation in Kirtland, Ohio, on 9 March 1833. He was revising the Bible and had finished the New Testament in February. He had reached the Apocrypha, books outside the Hebrew canon that some Bibles then included. He asked the Lord whether to revise those books too. Some Bible societies had recently stopped printing Bibles that contained them.
summary: The revelation answers a question about the Apocrypha. It says many things in those books are true and mostly translated correctly. It also says many things in them are not true but were added by human hands. The Apocrypha does not need to be translated. Whoever reads it should read with understanding, because “the Spirit manifesteth truth”. A reader enlightened by the Spirit will benefit, and one who is not will not.

contextNote.title: The Spirit as the reader’s filter
contextNote.text: The question was practical: should the revision include these extra books? Verses 1–2 give a mixed verdict, with truth and error side by side. Verse 3 settles the task by saying translation is “not needful”. Verse 4 shifts the work to the reader, because “the Spirit manifesteth truth”. Verses 5–6 state the result both ways: enlightened readers benefit, and others do not. In this passage, to understand means to tell true from false by the Spirit, not by a corrected edition.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 89–92 includes this short revelation on the Apocrypha. How could the test in verses 4–6 guide your reading of other books that mix truth and error?
reviewNote: Read all 6 verses. Official heading gives Kirtland, 9 March 1833, during Old Testament translation upon reaching the Apocrypha. JSP introduction read for the 2 February 1833 completion of the New Testament and the Bible societies’ removal of the Apocrypha. JSP does not name the Bible edition, so none is named here; Joseph apparently never revised the Apocrypha. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes
